rules.sentence: Fibrovascular tissue reaction is common, and when extensive, it leads to a diagnosis of sclerosing orbital pseudotumor.
Histopathological examination of orbital pseudotumor usually reveals a dense inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells, macrophages, and occasionally eosinophils.
Common histological findings seen in orbital pseudotumors include fibrosis and granulomatous reactions in addition to inflammatory infiltrates.

The granulomatous response is observed in several subtypes of orbital pseudotumor, including granulomatous orbital inflammation,[45] characterized by the production of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated large cells.
Granulomatous inflammation is uncommon, but a granulomatous inflammatory variant mimics sarcoidosis.
